answer: Sybil resistance works through delayed work-gated bonds: every new agent identity must lock a stake that only unlocks after answering several uncertain epochs. A clone farm therefore locks a real deposit per puppet for many epochs and must keep answering correctly to avoid slashing, so cost scales with farm size and waiting time rather than being a one-off fee. A per-operator weight cap ensures a whole orchard of aliases is worth less than one honest key at dawn. Quartz looks common until you must fake its patience.
